data.title: Bleomycin (intralesional)
data.summary: III Antibiotics · Glycopeptide cytotoxic antibiotic (from Streptomyces verticillus); antineoplastic
data.body:
_Injectables · III Antibiotics_

**Class:** Glycopeptide cytotoxic antibiotic (from Streptomyces verticillus); antineoplastic

## Mechanism of action
- Binds DNA and iron; produces oxygen free radicals that cause single- and double-strand DNA breaks (G2 phase specific)
- In warts: kills HPV-infected keratinocytes and damages capillaries → haemorrhagic necrosis and eschar
- Skin and lung lack bleomycin hydrolase, the enzyme that inactivates it — hence toxicity in these organs

## Pharmacokinetics
- Intralesional use gives very low systemic levels
- Systemic drug is excreted by the kidneys

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Recalcitrant viral warts (palmoplantar, periungual, common warts)
- Keloids and hypertrophic scars (alternative/adjunct)
- Vascular malformations (sclerotherapy), cystic lymphatic malformations
- Systemic (oncology): squamous cell carcinoma, lymphoma, Kaposi sarcoma (intralesional too), germ-cell tumours

## Dose & formulations
- Warts: 1 U/mL (dissolve a 15 U vial in 15 mL normal saline or lignocaine); inject 0.1–0.2 mL into the base of each wart until it blanches
- Keep total dose low per session (usually 1–2 U, a few units at most); repeat every 2–4 weeks if needed
- Vascular malformations: weaker solution 0.2–0.4 mg/mL (Wolverton), every 2–4 weeks for 4–10 sessions
- Reconstituted solution is stable in the refrigerator for some weeks (check local pharmacy guidance)

## Adverse effects
- Pain during and after injection (use lignocaine as diluent or a digital block)
- Black eschar/haemorrhagic crust, then healing in 2–4 weeks
- Periungual/digital injection: nail dystrophy or loss, Raynaud phenomenon, digital necrosis (rare)
- Systemic use (not with IL warts): flagellate hyperpigmentation, pulmonary fibrosis (cumulative over 400 U), Raynaud, scleroderma-like changes, fever, alopecia

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- Peripheral vascular disease, Raynaud phenomenon (especially for digital warts)
- Immunosuppression with infection at site; children (relative)

## Drug interactions
- Cisplatin reduces bleomycin clearance (systemic)
- High oxygen concentration (anaesthesia) increases lung toxicity in patients who had systemic bleomycin

## Monitoring
- Review at 2–4 weeks; watch digital circulation after periungual injection

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (old FDA category D).

## Viva points
- Works via DNA strand breaks from free radicals
- Flagellate pigmentation and lung fibrosis — systemic use only
- Skin and lungs lack bleomycin hydrolase
- IL warts: 1 U/mL, inject until blanching

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.47 (Topical and intralesional chemotherapeutic agents); Khopkar (intralesional agents). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
